en: To respect and admire someone because of their qualities or achievements.
ph: look up to a role model
ex: Many children look up to their parents.
許多孩子尊敬他們的父母。

en: To go back the way you came; or to return to an earlier point.
ex: The storm forced the climbers to turn back.
暴風雨迫使登山客折返。

en: To stay away from a class without permission.
ex: He got into trouble for cutting class.
他因為翹課而惹上麻煩。

en: Together with someone, often holding hands; or cooperating closely.
ex: The couple walked hand in hand along the beach.
這對情侶手牽手走在海灘上。

en: To put on clothes quickly and carelessly.
ex: He threw on a coat and ran out of the house.
他匆忙披上外套衝出了家門。

en: To be as good as something or someone expected; or to reach a particular level.
ex: The movie did not come up to my expectations.
這部電影沒有達到我的期待。

en: To examine something carefully; or to look at something from above.
ex: Please look over my essay before I hand it in.
在我交之前，請幫我看看這篇作文。

en: To know that someone or something exists; or to receive news about someone.
ex: Have you heard of this singer?
你聽說過這位歌手嗎？

en: To enter a place; or to become involved in a situation; or to start to be interested in something.
ex: He got into a lot of trouble at school.
他在學校惹了很多麻煩。

en: To stop employing someone because there is no work for them.
ex: The company laid off fifty workers last year.
公司去年裁掉了五十名員工。

en: To support someone and stay loyal to them; or to be ready to act.
ex: She stood by him through the hard times.
她在艱難時期一直支持他。

en: To become very angry or excited; or to become mentally ill.
ex: The crowd went mad when the band appeared.
樂團一出現，群眾就瘋狂了。

en: To make two people or groups compete or quarrel with each other for your own benefit.
col: play parents off against each other
play rivals off against each other
ex: He played the two companies off against each other.
他讓兩家公司彼此競爭。

en: To make something fall down by blowing it.
ex: The typhoon blew down hundreds of trees.
颱風吹倒了數百棵樹。

en: To make something shorter than planned; or to stop someone from continuing.
ex: The rain cut our picnic short.
一場雨使我們的野餐提早結束。

en: To do what you promised to do.
ex: She always keeps her word.
她總是信守承諾。

en: To be accepted as part of a group; or to be suitable or have enough time or space for something.
ex: It took him a while to fit in at his new school.
他花了一段時間才適應新學校。

en: To succeed in doing something difficult.
ex: He brought off the business deal successfully.
他成功地談成了這筆生意。

en: To give something to another person; or to continue to the next step; or to die.
ex: Please pass on my thanks to your parents.
請代我向你父母致謝。

en: To write something on paper; or to remove something by taking it apart.
ex: Let me take down your phone number.
讓我記下你的電話號碼。

en: To become less in amount or number; or to gradually disappear.
ex: Customer numbers began to drop away in winter.
冬天顧客數量開始減少。

en: To stop a fire from burning; or to make an effort; or to publish something.
ex: Firefighters quickly put out the fire.
消防員很快就把火撲滅了。

en: To remove something quickly; or to get rid of something unwanted.
ex: He threw off his coat as soon as he came in.
他一進門就脫掉了外套。

en: To produce something and make it available to the public; or to make a quality become noticeable.
ex: The company is bringing out a new smartphone next month.
公司下個月將推出新款智慧型手機。

en: To cause something to explode or fire; or to not punish someone severely.
ex: The boy was let off with a warning.
那個男孩只受到警告就被放過了。

en: To move to one side; or to not get involved in something.
ex: Please stand aside and let the doctor through.
請讓開，讓醫生過去。

en: To force a way through something; or to achieve an important advance.
ex: The sun finally broke through the clouds.
太陽終於穿透雲層。

en: To spend time in a particular place or with particular people, doing nothing in particular.
ex: We often hang out at the café on weekends.
我們週末常在咖啡店閒晃。

en: To happen in a particular way; or to be found to be something; or to switch off a light.
ex: The weather turned out to be perfect.
結果天氣好極了。

en: To separate by breaking; or to end a relationship or discussion suddenly.
ex: She broke off a piece of chocolate and gave it to me.
她掰下一塊巧克力給我。

en: To give something to someone younger, especially knowledge or traditions.
col: hand down from generation to generation
ex: This ring was handed down from my grandmother.
這枚戒指是從我祖母傳下來的。

en: To say what is true and not lie.
ex: Always tell the truth, even if it's hard.
即使很難，也要說實話。

en: To stop living because of a particular illness, injury or condition.
ex: Many people in the region die of hunger.
該地區許多人死於飢餓。

en: To watch someone or something carefully.
col: keep an eye on the baby
keep an eye on the time
ex: Could you keep an eye on my bag for a minute?
你能幫我看一下包包嗎？

en: To depend on someone or something; or to be sure that something will happen.
ex: You can count on me to help.
你可以指望我幫忙。

en: To write a short letter or message to someone.
col: drop a line to a friend
ex: Drop me a line when you get there.
你到了之後寫封短信給我。

en: To become angry and shout or behave badly.
ex: He rarely loses his temper.
他很少發脾氣。

en: To meet someone by chance; or to hit something accidentally.
ex: I bumped into my teacher at the mall.
我在購物中心偶遇我的老師。

en: To produce or cause something; or to put forward an idea.
ex: The discussion brought forth many new ideas.
這場討論產生了許多新想法。

en: To listen to or look at someone or something carefully.
ex: Please pay attention to the instructions.
請注意聽說明。
